label: Kitting
info: MAIN FLOW – Kitting integration between Mendix, Node-RED and PLC DB116. Mendix submits work orders to the FIFO queue. The PLC release signal requests one container. Node-RED writes 19 DB116 values, verifies them by read-back, and then raises the New Data trigger. PLC Data Received ACK changes the queue record to sent. Kitting Started and Kitting Completed events are posted to Mendix. A successful Completed response advances the container queue. The lower section caches PLC Step-4 IDs and initializes/recover queue state. Configure the PLC endpoint and Mendix URL before deployment. Persistent queue recovery requires localfilesystem context storage.

name: COE HTTP POST (retry)
info:
Generic JSON POST with bounded retry.

**Input** msg.url, msg.payload (object), msg.label (log tag)

**Output 1** success (msg.httpOk = true, msg.statusCode)

**Output 2** failed after MAX_ATTEMPTS (msg.httpOk = false, msg.httpError, msg.attempts)

Success = HTTP 200/201/202/204 (same rule as the Python http_post()).

name: Mendix → Edge: store batch atomically in PostgreSQL
info: Validation = Pydantic equivalent (HTTP 422 on bad body). Insert = ONE SQL statement with data-modifying CTEs, so badge + containers + details are stored atomically (replaces explicit commit/rollback).

name: Validate (422 on error)
Store batch (atomic CTE)
query:
WITH p AS (SELECT $1::jsonb AS j),
b AS (
    INSERT INTO badges (badge_id, batch_id, queue_status)
    SELECT j->>'badge_id', j->>'batch_id', 'pending' FROM p
    ON CONFLICT (badge_id) DO UPDATE SET batch_id = EXCLUDED.batch_id, queue_status = 'pending'
    RETURNING badge_id
),
c AS (
    INSERT INTO containers (badge_id, container_name, pallet_id, part_a_type, part_b_type, rack_id, final_product_name)
    SELECT b.badge_id, ct->>'container_name', ct->>'pallet_id', ct->>'partA_type', ct->>'partB_type',
           ct->>'rack_id', ct->>'final_product_name'
    FROM b, p, jsonb_array_elements(p.j->'containers') AS ct
    ON CONFLICT (badge_id, container_name) DO UPDATE
        SET pallet_id = EXCLUDED.pallet_id, part_a_type = EXCLUDED.part_a_type, part_b_type = EXCLUDED.part_b_type,
            rack_id = EXCLUDED.rack_id, final_product_name = EXCLUDED.final_product_name
    RETURNING id, container_name
),
d_del AS (
    DELETE FROM details WHERE container_id IN (SELECT id FROM c) RETURNING 1
),
d_ins AS (
    INSERT INTO details (container_id, operation_name, task_name, task_sequence)
    SELECT c.id, t->>'operation_name', t->>'task_name', (t->>'task_sequence')::int
    FROM p
    CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(p.j->'containers') AS ct
    JOIN c ON c.container_name = ct->>'container_name'
    CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(ct->'tasks') AS t
    RETURNING 1
)
SELECT (SELECT badge_id FROM b) AS badge_id,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM badges WHERE queue_status = 'pending' AND badge_id <> (SELECT badge_id FROM b)) + 1 AS pending_count,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM c) AS containers_stored,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM d_ins) AS tasks_stored;

name: DB116 handshake: release_new_data → claim → write → VERIFY → new_data_trigger
info:
1. PLC sets **release_new_data** (rising edge) – or a previous request is still *waiting* because the queue was empty.
2. Node claims the oldest *pending* badge (UPDATE … 'processing') and reads its first container + task details in the same statement.
3. All data fields are written to DB116 in ONE multi-variable write.
4. Next 1-second scan: the bridge READS BACK the DB116 fields. Only when they match what was written is **new_data_trigger** set.
   (The Python service set the trigger immediately, even if a write had failed.) If verification fails for 10 s the badge goes back to 'pending'.
5. PLC sets **data_received_ack** → badge becomes 'sent'.
6. **kitting_start_trigger / kitting_complete_trigger** → Mendix kitting status.

name: Kitting bridge (edges + state)
Claim next pending badge
query:
WITH nxt AS (
    SELECT b.badge_id FROM badges b
    WHERE b.queue_status = 'pending'
      AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM containers c WHERE c.badge_id = b.badge_id)
    ORDER BY b.created_at ASC
    LIMIT 1
    FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
),
claimed AS (
    UPDATE badges b SET queue_status = 'processing' FROM nxt
    WHERE b.badge_id = nxt.badge_id
    RETURNING b.badge_id, b.batch_id
)
SELECT cl.badge_id, cl.batch_id, c.container_name, c.pallet_id, c.part_a_type, c.part_b_type, c.rack_id,
       COALESCE((SELECT json_agg(json_build_object('operation_name', d.operation_name,
                                                   'task_name', d.task_name,
                                                   'task_sequence', d.task_sequence)
                                 ORDER BY d.operation_name, d.task_sequence)
                 FROM details d WHERE d.container_id = c.id), '[]'::json) AS details,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM badges WHERE queue_status = 'pending') - 1 AS pending_after
FROM claimed cl
JOIN LATERAL (SELECT * FROM containers WHERE badge_id = cl.badge_id ORDER BY id LIMIT 1) c ON true;

DB113 trigger → read data → ACK to PLC → POST to Mendix
info:
| Trigger | Python class | Mendix endpoint | PLC ACK (written BEFORE the POST, as in Python) |
|---|---|---|---|
| DBX0.0 StationStartTrigger | S1_MoveInMonitor | operation_status {Started:true, Completed:false} | DBX772.0 |
| DBX0.1 StationCompleteTrigger | S1_MoveOutMonitor | operation_status {Started:false, Completed:true} | DBX772.1 |
| DBX774.0 ProcessDataTrigger | S1_BoltDataMonitor | bolt_data {Torque, Angle} | DBX1556.0 |

The detector receives the whole DB113 image in ONE message, so the strings/ints it reads belong to the same scan as the trigger bit (no read-after-trigger race).

name: Detector DB113
Mendix verified the scanned part QR → PLC may continue
info: Writes DB113.DBX772.2 (PartScanACK). Returns HTTP 500 when the PLC link is down (Python: when the write failed).

name: Validate + write PartScanACK
Error → HTTP 500 / registry
DB3 triggers
info:
| Trigger | Mendix endpoint | PLC ACK |
|---|---|---|
| DBX0.0 STATION_START_TRIG | operation_status {Started:true} | DBX772.0 written first |
| DBX774.0 PROCESS_DATA_TRIG | press_data {Torque = force N, Angle = depth mm} | DBX1554.0 written first |
| DBX0.1 STATION_COMPLETE_TRIG | operation_status {Completed:true} | DBX772.1 written ONLY after Mendix answered OK |

Move-out uses 3 attempts (2 s apart) because the ACK depends on the POST – a transient network error would otherwise leave the PLC waiting for ever.

name: Detector DB3
ACK after Mendix OK
Error → registry
DB45 triggers
info:
| Trigger | Mendix endpoint | PLC ACK (before POST) |
|---|---|---|
| DBX0.0 station_start | operation_status {Started, Completed = live bits} | DBX772.0 |
| DBX774.0 process_data | parameterlist List {OverAll, Bolt1-5, Bearing, BearingSize, PartColour} | DBX1550.0 |
| DBX0.1 station_complete | operation_status {Started, Completed = live bits} | DBX772.1 |

**Sequence number:** the Python code read DB45 offsets 770 / 1544 as a *string*, which can never match the INT layout used by the other stations, so it always fell back to 1 (move) / 2 (vision). Here they are read as INT; if the PLC value is not a plausible task sequence (1…999) the same fallback (1 / 2) is used. See LLD finding F1.

name: Detector DB45
Mendix → PLC: UserOK (DBX772.2) / UserNOK (DBX772.3)
info: Exactly one bit is set, the opposite one is cleared (two writes in a fixed order). Both false → HTTP 400. The PLC resets the bits itself (as before).

query:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS badges (
    id           SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    badge_id     VARCHAR(100) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    batch_id     VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    queue_status VARCHAR(20)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',
    created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS containers (
    id                 SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    badge_id           VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL REFERENCES badges(badge_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    container_name     VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    pallet_id          VARCHAR(100),
    part_a_type        VARCHAR(100),
    part_b_type        VARCHAR(100),
    rack_id            VARCHAR(100),
    final_product_name VARCHAR(200),
    created_at         TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
    UNIQUE(badge_id, container_name)
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS details (
    id             SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    container_id   INT NOT NULL REFERENCES containers(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    operation_name VARCHAR(200),
    task_name      VARCHAR(200),
    task_sequence  INT,
    created_at     TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_badges_queue ON badges (queue_status, created_at);

To start docker with a bind mount volume (-v option), for example:

```
docker run -it -p 1880:1880 -v /home/user/node_red_data:/data --name mynodered nodered/node-red
```

where `/home/user/node_red_data` is a directory on your host machine where you want to store your flows.

If you do not do this then you can experiment and redploy flows, but if you restart or upgrade the container the flows will be disconnected and lost. 

They will still exist in a hidden data volume, which can be recovered using standard docker techniques, but that is much more complex than just starting with a named volume as described above.

Cache & Deliver Task
info:
The Cache & Deliver Task Function stores the incoming
task details in AMR_TASKS,records its initial status
and received time, prepares the POST request with the 
task information, and forwards it to the AMR for execution.

name: Format Task Response
info:
Checks the AMR HTTP response status and sends a 
success or error response with the TaskId back to
Mendix.

name: Conveyor Interlock & Command
info:
Validates the TaskId and conveyor details, checks the AMR 
endpoint, prepares the conveyor command, and sends it to AMR.
It also sends an immediate acknowledgement to Mendix and logs
the command for monitoring.

name: Update Status & Forward Mendix
info:
Receives AMR task status updates, validates the TaskId 
and Order_Status, updates the stored task status, and 
forwards the update to Mendix. It also sends an immediate
acknowledgement to AMR and logs the status update.

name: Station 1 Drop Interlock
info:
Prepares the PLC drop-position command, sends the drop confirmation 
to Mendix, and returns an immediate acknowledgement.

name: Clean & Forward AMR Health
info:
Receives AMR health data, cleans and standardizes the health
status fields, retrieves the Mendix endpoint, and forwards 
the cleaned data to Mendix. It also checks endpoint configuration, 
sends an immediate acknowledgement to AMR, and returns an 
error if the Mendix endpoint is missing.

name: Validate Task Details
info:
The Validate Task Details node checks whether 
the incoming task from Mendix contains all three
required fields: TaskId, source and destination.
If all three are present, it forwards the task 
to Cache & Deliver Task. If any field is missing
or empty, it sends an error response (HTTP 400) 
back to Mendix.

name: Catch AMR Task Errors
info:
Captures errors occurring during the 
AMR task API request and forwards 
error details to the Debug sidebar 
for monitoring and troubleshooting.

name: Validate Station 1 Drop
info:
Checks whether station1_drop_position is provided before allowing 
the request to proceed to the PLC. If missing, returns HTTP 400 
with an error message.

name: Catch Station 1 Drop Errors
info:
Captures errors from the Station 1 Drop 
Function and PLC output node and forwards 
them to Debug for troubleshooting.

name: Process Batch & Queue
List Badges
View Queue
Mark Processing Badge as Sent
Fetch Pending & Write All DB116 Registers
Store step4_container_id
Store step4_batch_id
Read PLC DB116 & Format Started
Read PLC DB116 & Format Completed
DB116.DBX0.0 (release_new_data)
info: PLC INPUT – Monitors DB116.DBX0.0 (release_new_data). The S7 input is configured for change detection; the following switch allows only TRUE through to request the next container.

name: Rising Edge (True)
info: PLC EVENT FILTER – Passes only TRUE for DB116 release_new_data. The PLC must reset the bit before another rising event can be processed.

name: Fetch Pending & Write All DB116 Registers
info: FIFO WRITER – Finds the oldest pending badge, reserves its current container as processing, builds the 19 named DB116 values in the configured order, and sends them to the S7 output. It waits if another badge is active or the queue is empty. It records the expected values and retry limits for the read-back verification node. NewData is not triggered here; verification must succeed first.

name: Write DB116 Data Registers
info: PLC OUTPUT – Writes the 19 DB116 data variables supplied by Fetch Pending & Write All DB116 Registers. Confirm on the installed node-red-contrib-s7 version that the configured variable-array/payload-array message format is supported before production use.

name: DB116 all values (write read-back)
info: PLC READ-BACK INPUT – Reads the configured S7 variable table as one object. Verify Write -> Trigger compares this data with the 19 expected values and triggers the PLC only after a match. This mode and payload shape must match the installed node-red-contrib-s7 version.

name: Verify Write -> Trigger
info: WRITE VERIFICATION – Compares every expected DB116 value against the PLC read-back. If all 19 match, Output 1 raises DB116_new_data_trigger. If the verification timeout expires, Output 2 retries the data write up to the configured maximum. After the final failure it marks the badge write_failed and does not trigger the PLC. A PLC-side sequence/handshake is recommended to avoid accepting stale values that happen to match.

name: DB116.DBX514.0 = True
info: PLC OUTPUT – Sets DB116.DBX514.0 (New Data Trigger) TRUE only after all 19 data values have passed read-back verification. The PLC program must reset this trigger according to the agreed handshake.

name: Next container (kick)
info: INTERNAL LINK INPUT – Receives a kick from a newly submitted batch or a successfully completed container. It wakes the FIFO writer without creating another HTTP request or directly writing PLC data.

name: kick: new batch
info: INTERNAL LINK OUTPUT – Sends a kick after a batch is accepted when the PLC writer is already waiting for queue data.

name: DB116.DBX0.1 (data_received_ack)
info: PLC INPUT – Monitors DB116.DBX0.1 (data_received_ack). A TRUE transition is filtered and passed to the queue acknowledgement handler. This ACK means the PLC accepted the transferred data; it does not mean kitting is complete.

name: Rising Edge (True)
info: PLC EVENT FILTER – Passes only TRUE for DB116 data_received_ack. The PLC must reset the ACK bit before another acknowledgement event.

name: Mark Processing Badge as Sent
info: QUEUE ACK HANDLER – Confirms that no write verification is still pending, finds the processing badge, and changes its status to sent. It records the PLC acknowledgement timestamp and container index. An ACK received before verification or without a processing badge is ignored and logged.

name: DB116.DBX0.2 (kitting_start_trigger)
info: PLC INPUT – Monitors DB116.DBX0.2 (kitting_start_trigger). A TRUE transition indicates that the PLC has started processing the loaded container and is sent to the Started payload builder.

name: Rising Edge (True)
info: PLC EVENT FILTER – Passes only TRUE for DB116 kitting_start_trigger so one Started event is generated per PLC 0-to-1 transition. The PLC must reset the bit for the next cycle.

name: Read PLC DB116 & Format Started
info: MENDIX STARTED PAYLOAD BUILDER – Identifies the active badge/container, uses the Step-4 ID cache when available, attaches the batch/container identifiers and builds the Mendix status JSON. For this node the payload must be Started=true and Completed=false. It sends the request to the Started HTTP Request node.

name: POST kitting_status (Started)
info: HTTP REQUEST – POSTs the Started event JSON to the Mendix kitting status endpoint configured in Load Persistent Queue & Flag In-Flight Orders. The HTTP response is passed to Check Mendix Response.

name: DB116.DBX0.3 (kitting_complete_trigger)
info: PLC INPUT – Monitors DB116.DBX0.3 (kitting_complete_trigger). A TRUE transition indicates that the PLC has completed the current container and is sent to the Completed payload builder.

name: Rising Edge (True)
info: PLC EVENT FILTER – Passes only TRUE for DB116 kitting_complete_trigger so one Completed event is generated per PLC 0-to-1 transition. The PLC must reset the bit for the next cycle.

name: Read PLC DB116 & Format Completed
info: MENDIX COMPLETED PAYLOAD BUILDER – Identifies the active badge/container, uses the Step-4 ID cache when available, attaches the batch/container identifiers and builds the Mendix status JSON. For this node the payload must be Started=false and Completed=true. It sends the request to the Completed HTTP Request node.

name: POST kitting_status (Completed)
info: HTTP REQUEST – POSTs the Completed event JSON to the Mendix kitting status endpoint. Check Mendix Response advances the queue only after an accepted successful HTTP response. A failed request is reported and does not advance the queue; arrange a retry/reconciliation if the endpoint can be temporarily unavailable.

name: Check Mendix Response
info: MENDIX RESPONSE HANDLER – Accepts HTTP 200, 201, 202 or 204. Failed responses are logged and do not change the queue. A successful Started response only reports the event result. A successful Completed response advances the matching container index, marks the badge completed when all containers are done, and sends a kick if the PLC was waiting. Output 1 goes to Debug; Output 2 wakes the FIFO writer.

name: Debug: Mendix result
info: DEBUG OUTPUT – Displays the result of each Started or Completed Mendix status request, including HTTP success or failure.

name: kick: container completed
info: INTERNAL LINK OUTPUT – Sends a kick after a successful container completion when the PLC had already requested the next container while the previous container was active.

name: Read DB116.S2.40 (step4_container_id)
info: PLC INPUT – Reads the Step-4 container ID from DB116.S2.40 (DB116_step4_container_id). This value is cached for status reporting and checked against the active queue container.

name: Store step4_container_id
info: STEP-4 CACHE – Stores the latest container ID read from the PLC in flow context under step4.container. The cache is a fallback/reference for the Mendix status payload, not the primary queue record.

name: Read DB116.S258.40 (step4_batch_id)
info: PLC INPUT – Reads the Step-4 batch ID from DB116.S258.40 (DB116_step4_batch_id). This value is cached for status reporting.

name: Store step4_batch_id
info: STEP-4 CACHE – Stores the latest batch ID read from the PLC in flow context under step4.batch. The cache is a fallback/reference for the Mendix status payload, not the primary queue record.

name: On Start: Recover Queue
info: STARTUP INJECT – Runs once shortly after Node-RED starts/deploys and calls the queue/configuration recovery function.

name: Load Persistent Queue & Flag In-Flight Orders
info: STARTUP AND RECOVERY – Loads the Mendix endpoint and queue settings, creates WO_QUEUE if it does not exist, initializes the waiting flag, and recovers records left in processing after restart by returning them to pending. Records already sent remain active until a completion event. Persistent recovery requires localfilesystem context storage; after a restart, compare the PLC state with GET /queue before resuming production.

name: 1 | MENDIX -> EDGE : receive batch & expose queue
info:
Why: Mendix pushes a work order (badge + batch + containers + tasks). Edge validates it and puts it in the queue as 'pending'.
The PLC will pull it later when it raises release_new_data (section 2).
Test:
curl -X POST http://<edge>:1880/submit-batch -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @Work_Order_sample.json

name: POST /submit-batch
info: Entry point for Mendix work orders. JSON body: {badge_id, batch_id, containers:[{container_name, pallet_id, partA_type, partB_type, rack_id, final_product_name, tasks:[{operation_name, task_name, task_sequence}]}]}

name: Process Batch & Queue
info: Validates payload, upserts it in WO_QUEUE (status pending), answers Mendix, and wakes the PLC writer if the PLC was waiting for data.

name: HTTP Response
info: Answers Mendix with the status code and JSON prepared by 'Process Batch & Queue' (200 accepted, 422 invalid, 409 badge already active).

name: GET /badges
info: Returns the complete queue incl. containers & tasks (debug/monitoring).

name: GET /queue
info: Returns a short queue summary: badge_id, batch_id, queue_status, created_at.

name: List Queue
info: Reads WO_QUEUE and returns either the full list (/badges) or the summary (/queue).

name: 2 | PLC SIGNALS : read the 4 DB116 trigger bits
info:
Why: the S7 nodes poll the PLC every 200 ms (endpoint cycle time) and only emit when a bit CHANGES (diff = true).
'Rising Edge' keeps only TRUE (0->1) so every trigger acts exactly once. 'Route by Tag' sends each signal to its own handler.
Bits: DBX0.0 release_new_data | DBX0.1 data_received_ack | DBX0.2 kitting_start | DBX0.3 kitting_complete

name: 3 | EDGE -> PLC : take next pending badge and write DB116
info:
Why: write ALL data registers first, THEN raise NewData Trigger (DBX514.0) after a short delay, so the PLC never sees the trigger before the data is complete.
If the queue is empty the request is remembered ('waiting') and served automatically when Mendix submits the next batch.

name: 4 | PLC ACK : Data Received -> badge becomes SENT
info: PLC sets DB116.DBX0.1 HIGH only after all 19 data values are copied/validated. The ACK Function accepts one HIGH per container, records the timestamp, and changes queue_status processing -> sent. PLC must reset DBX0.1 LOW before the next container. This ACK confirms data receipt only; DBX0.3 / Mendix Completed is a separate process-completion event.

name: 5 | KITTING STATUS -> MENDIX
info:
Why: Mendix must know when kitting started and completed for the container/batch currently in the PLC.
IDs are read from the PLC (DB116 step-4 strings, cached below); if empty we fall back to the active badge in the queue.
After Mendix confirms 'completed', the badge is closed in the queue.

name: 0 | CONFIG & INIT (runs once on deploy/start)
info: Why: all settings live in ONE place and the queue always exists before the first request or PLC signal arrives.
